how-to-wash-a-wool-sweater:
By Kristine, Autumn & Wool, Riga · Updated 25 November 2026

Hand wash a wool sweater in cool water with a mild wool detergent. Press it gently, never wring or twist it, and dry it flat on a towel away from heat. Store it folded, not hung. Check the care line on your product page first.
merino-vs-lambswool:
By Kristine, Autumn & Wool, Riga · Updated 25 November 2026

Merino is a finer wool that feels smooth against the skin, so it suits next-to-skin layers. Lambswool comes from young sheep and feels soft and springy. Neither is automatically warmer: yarn weight and knit decide warmth. Both need the same gentle hand wash. Pick by the feel you want.
oversized-fit-guide:
By Kristine, Autumn & Wool, Riga · Updated 25 November 2026

Choose your size from your chest, waist and hip measurements, then check the garment width on the product page. Double the flat width to get the full circumference and compare it with your chest. The difference is your ease, the extra room. Vests and many oversized pieces come in one size.
how-to-choose-a-wool-cardigan:
By Kristine, Autumn & Wool, Riga · Updated 25 November 2026

Choose a wool cardigan by style, length and fibre. Open-front is the simple straight line, shawl collar is longer and softer, and raglan is the easy everyday fit. Our four cardigans cost €145 to €160 and are 100% new wool or 100% merino. Check garment length and the material line before ordering.
